config.title: WebSocket Hook

intro.title: WebSocket Hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook named `useWebSocket` to manage WebSocket connections in a React application. You will learn how to create a reusable hook that handles WebSocket events like opening, receiving messages, and closing. The core concepts involve using React hooks such as `useState` and `useEffect` to manage state and side effects. You will implement this in TypeScript to ensure type safety for WebSocket data and events. By the end, you'll have a functional hook that can connect to a WebSocket server and update your UI in real-time.
intro.usecase: WebSocket hooks are essential for building real-time features in modern web applications. You'll see them powering live chat interfaces like Slack or Discord, where messages appear instantly without page refreshes. They're also crucial for financial dashboards that display live stock prices, collaborative editing tools like Google Docs showing simultaneous changes, and multiplayer gaming interfaces that update player positions in real-time. As a developer, you'll implement WebSocket hooks whenever your application needs to maintain persistent connections for instant data synchronization between client and server.

objectives: Implement a custom React hook to manage WebSocket connections.
Initialize a WebSocket instance and manage its lifecycle within a hook.
Configure the hook to handle incoming messages and update component state.
Bind the custom hook to a React component to display real-time data.
Control the WebSocket connection by opening and closing it based on component events.
Integrate TypeScript interfaces to define the structure of WebSocket message data.
Manipulate state to reflect connection status and message history.

steps.title: Define WebSocket hook interface for type safety
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named 'UseWebSocketReturn' that defines the return type for your custom WebSocket hook. Include properties for connection status (isConnected: boolean), messages (messages: string[]), a send function (send: (message: string) => void), and connection controls (connect: () => void, disconnect: () => void).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define each property with its type. Remember that functions should have parameter types and return type annotations.

// Define the UseWebSocketReturn interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a TypeScript interface that clearly defines the shape of the object your custom WebSocket hook will return, ensuring type safety throughout your component.
successCriteria: An interface named 'UseWebSocketReturn' is defined with properties: isConnected (boolean), messages (string[]), send (function that takes string and returns void), connect (function that returns void), and disconnect (function that returns void).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Create custom useWebSocket hook function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'useWebSocket' that takes a 'url' parameter of type string and returns the UseWebSocketReturn interface type. Start with the function skeleton that returns an empty object cast to UseWebSocketReturn.
steps.hint: Define a function with the signature (url: string): UseWebSocketReturn. Inside, return an empty object {} as UseWebSocketReturn for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: A useWebSocket function is defined with proper TypeScript typing, ready to be implemented in later steps.
successCriteria: The useWebSocket function is created with a url parameter of type string and returns UseWebSocketReturn.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but check the parameter type or return type to match the interface.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or has incorrect typing. Ensure it takes a string url and returns UseWebSocketReturn.

steps.instruction: Inside the useWebSocket hook, use useState to create two state variables: isConnected (boolean) and messages (string array). Add proper TypeScript type annotations for both.
steps.hint: Remember to call useState with initial values and destructure the array to get the state variable and setter function for each.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useWebSocket hook will have properly typed state variables to track connection status and message history.
successCriteria: The useWebSocket hook contains useState calls for isConnected (boolean) and messages (string array) with correct TypeScript type annotations.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that both state variables have proper TypeScript annotations and initial values. Make sure isConnected is boolean and messages is string[].
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Inside the useWebSocket hook, use useState to create isConnected (boolean) and messages (string array) with TypeScript types.

steps.title: Create WebSocket instance reference
steps.instruction: Inside the useWebSocket hook, create a wsRef using the useRef hook to store the WebSocket instance. Type it as WebSocket | null and initialize it with null.
steps.hint: useRef is perfect for storing mutable values that shouldn't trigger re-renders when they change. Initialize it with null since no connection exists yet.

// Similar: storing a DOM element reference
const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement | null>(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: A wsRef variable is created using useRef, properly typed to hold a WebSocket instance or null.
successCriteria: The useWebSocket hook contains a wsRef variable created with useRef<WebSocket | null>(null).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to use useRef with the correct type annotation (WebSocket | null) and initialize it with null.

steps.title: Define WebSocket connection handler
steps.instruction: Inside the useWebSocket hook, define a connect function using useCallback that will create a WebSocket instance, set up event listeners, and update the connection state.
steps.hint: Use useCallback to memoize the connect function. Inside it, create a new WebSocket instance, assign it to the ref, and set up event listeners for 'open', 'message', and 'close' events.
steps.expectedOutcome: The connect function is defined with useCallback, creating a WebSocket instance, setting up event listeners, and updating the isConnected state.
successCriteria: A connect function is defined using useCallback, creates a WebSocket instance, sets up event listeners for 'open', 'message', and 'close' events, and updates the isConnected state appropriately.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the connect function, but make sure to use useCallback, create the WebSocket instance, and set up all three event listeners.
steps.feedbackWrong: The connect function is missing or incomplete. It should be defined with useCallback and handle WebSocket connection setup.

steps.title: Define WebSocket disconnection handler
steps.instruction: Inside the useWebSocket hook, define a disconnect function using useCallback that properly closes the WebSocket connection and updates the connection state.
steps.hint: Use useCallback to memoize the disconnect function. Inside it, check if the WebSocket instance exists and is open, then call its close method and update isConnected state to false.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useWebSocket hook now includes a properly implemented disconnect function that closes the WebSocket connection and updates the connection state.
successCriteria: A disconnect function is defined using useCallback, checks if the WebSocket instance exists, calls close() on it, and updates isConnected state to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your disconnect function uses useCallback, checks if the WebSocket exists, calls close(), and updates the isConnected state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The disconnect function isn't properly implemented. It should use useCallback, check the WebSocket instance, close it, and update the connection state.

steps.title: Define message sending handler
steps.instruction: Inside the useWebSocket hook, define a sendMessage function using useCallback that sends data through the WebSocket if connected.
steps.hint: Use useCallback to memoize the function. Check if the WebSocket instance exists and its readyState is OPEN before sending.
steps.expectedOutcome: A sendMessage function is defined inside the hook, ready to be used for sending messages.
successCriteria: The sendMessage function is defined with useCallback, checks WebSocket connection state, and calls send on the WebSocket instance.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a sendMessage function, but it might be missing useCallback or the connection check.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sendMessage function is not defined correctly. Make sure to use useCallback and check the WebSocket readyState.

steps.title: Set up WebSocket lifecycle with useEffect
steps.instruction: Inside the useWebSocket hook, add a useEffect hook that calls the connect function when the component mounts and returns a cleanup function that calls disconnect.
steps.hint: The useEffect should have an empty dependency array to run only on mount, and its return function should handle cleanup.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect hook is added to manage the WebSocket connection lifecycle, ensuring proper setup and cleanup.
successCriteria: The useEffect hook is implemented with an empty dependency array, calls connect inside, and returns a cleanup function that calls disconnect.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the useEffect has an empty dependency array and includes both the connect call and a cleanup function that calls disconnect.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useEffect hook for WebSocket lifecycle management is missing or incorrect. Remember to add useEffect with an empty dependency array, call connect inside it, and return a cleanup function that calls disconnect.

steps.instruction: Complete the custom hook by returning an object containing the isConnected state, messages array, sendMessage function, connect function, and disconnect function from your useWebSocket hook.
